points.text: chlorine green ; bromine brown ; iodine (dark) grey
points.guidance: All three correct for one mark

points.text: M3: (so) increased strength of instantaneous dipole – induced dipole forces (of attraction)
($\text{Br}_2$ / bromine is an) oxidising agent AND removes electron(s) from iodide (ions) $\text{I}^-$ OR increases the oxidation number of $\text{I}^-$ / iodide (ion)
M2: $\text{Cl}^-$ is not a strong enough reducing agent to reduce $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
points.guidance: Alternative M2: ability to behave as reducing agents increases down the group

points.text: M3: $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$ are strong enough reducing agents to react (further) with (the S in) $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
points.guidance: Alternative M3: EITHER $\text{Cl}^-$ is not strong enough to reduce $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ OR $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$ react (further) with (the S in) $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
